question: Is the visitor record I got when I extended my stay the same thing as a Canadian visitor visa?
generated_answer:
When you extended your stay in Canada, you likely received a visitor record, which is a document that confirms your temporary resident status in Canada. While a visitor record and a Canadian visitor visa are related, they are not exactly the same thing.

A Canadian visitor visa, also known as a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV), is a document that allows a foreign national to enter Canada for a specific period. It's usually issued by a Canadian visa office outside of Canada and is required for citizens of certain countries.

On the other hand, a visitor record is a document issued by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) or the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) when a foreign national enters Canada or extends their stay. It confirms the conditions of their stay, including the length of time they're allowed to remain in Canada and any restrictions on their activities.

If you're already in Canada and extend your stay, you'll typically receive a visitor record, which will outline the new terms of your stay. This document is usually issued by IRCC or CBSA, and it's proof of your temporary resident status in Canada.

To summarize:

* A Canadian visitor visa (TRV) is required for entry into Canada and is usually issued outside of Canada.
* A visitor record is issued when you enter Canada or extend your stay, and it confirms the conditions of your temporary resident status in Canada.

I hope that helps clarify the difference! If you have any more questions or concerns, feel free to ask.
